page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, supported by a 40 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a 4.0 GB per core allocation. Acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA Pascal P4 GPU equipped with 8 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the CPU and memory subsystems operate in lower percentiles compared to modern hardware. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 953.38 falls into the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 4755.08 is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak results, with large block read-only speeds at 37.18 GB/sec and write speeds at 25.34 GB/sec. PassMark CPU testing yields an average score of 6698.53, though extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests consistently register in the bottom 25%. Database operations and Redis SET performance also reflect these constraints, with Redis achieving 5.48 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance utilizes older-generation Intel Broadwell and NVIDIA Pascal architectures. This hardware profile offers a lower-cost entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads that do not require modern tensor cores or high-bandwidth memory. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which must be factored into overall architecture planning. The instance is suitable for entry-level GPU workloads, legacy CUDA applications, basic video transcoding, and lightweight machine learning inference where high-throughput CPU performance is not a primary bottleneck.
